findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in ADR 0125 decision 6 how the MCP server's three keys reach its environment: either literal values in the repo-tracked infra files (and why that is not repo pinning), or injection from host/secret configuration that those files only reference.
evidence: Context: "The operator decided ... that op-cert keys must not be hardcoded in the repository."
Decision 6: "configured through its deployment (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`) with the 3 keys the operator listed"

Decision 3: the list is "held in the verifying environment's own configuration (user config, env var, deployment, or a CI job's protected variables); the repository's `rebar.toml` does not set it" — this excludes only rebar.toml, not other repo-tracked files.
findings.finding: Decision item 6 says the MCP server's three trusted keys are configured through `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` and `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`. These are repository files. The plan does not say whether the key material is written literally into them or injected from host/secret configuration. Literal keys there would recreate repository-pinned keys, which the Context says the operator ruled out.
findings.location: Approach → Decision item 6; Context ('op-cert keys must not be hardcoded in the repository')
scenarios: The later deployment story pastes the three base64 keys into docker-compose.yml, so the keys are hardcoded in the repo again, contrary to the epic.
An ADR reader cannot tell whether committing keys to infra/ is sanctioned by ADR 0125.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword decision 6 along these lines: "Rebar's MCP server receives `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` through its deployment; `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` and `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` pass the variable from the host's deployment environment/secret store, and no key material is committed." Identify the three keys by env_id and comment (optionally by SHA256 fingerprint) rather than by base64 material. If the operator really intends literal values in compose, say so explicitly and explain how that differs from the rejected 'keep the repo pin file' alternative.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In ADR 0125 Decision item 6, state whether the MCP server's trusted-key list lives as literals in repo-tracked deployment files or is injected from an out-of-repo source (host env/secret), and reconcile that with the 'no keys hardcoded in the repository' rule.
evidence: "The operator decided ... that op-cert keys must not be hardcoded in the repository."
"Rebar's MCP server is configured through its deployment (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`) with the 3 keys the operator listed"
"the repository's `rebar.toml` does not set it" — only rebar.toml is excluded; repo-tracked deployment files are not
findings.finding: Decision item 6 configures the MCP server's three trusted op-cert keys through `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` and `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`. Both are repository files, so committing the key literals there would contradict the operator's decision that op-cert keys must not be hardcoded in the repository. Item 3 rules out only `rebar.toml` as a location. The ADR does not say whether these deployment files carry the keys or only pass through a value supplied from outside the repository.
findings.location: Approach > Decision item 6 (and item 3 'the repository's rebar.toml does not set it')
scenarios: A later story follows ADR 0125 literally and commits the three `nava-opcert-prod`/`rebar-opcert` key lines into docker-compose.yml. That recreates a repo-pinned trust root under a different filename, which is the outcome the epic exists to remove.
A reviewer cannot tell from the ADR whether a key literal in autodeploy.sh complies with the decision or violates it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a deterministic check to AC1 that greps docs/adr/0125-opcert-trust-per-environment.md for each required header value, section heading and token, and tighten AC3 to show the ADR 0125 notes sit next to ADR 0104 decision 3 and its env_id note.
evidence: AC1: "its Decision states items 1-6, including `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`, `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS`, the entry format, `untrusted`, `trust_list`, `signing_key` ... (checked by reading the merged file)"
AC3: "`git grep -c 'ADR 0125' -- docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` is at least 2"
findings.finding: AC1 is verified only "by reading the merged file". That is a subjective prose check, although the AC lists exact literal tokens that could be checked deterministically. The 0104 check `git grep -c 'ADR 0125' ... is at least 2` counts matching lines anywhere in the file. It does not confirm the notes sit at decision 3 and at the env_id note.
scenarios: An ADR that omits `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` or the `Status: Accepted` header passes AC1 because no command asserts the token.
Two 'ADR 0125' mentions placed together at the top of ADR 0104 satisfy AC3 without annotating decision 3 or the env_id note.
findings.suggested_fix: For AC1, add: `for t in 'Status: Accepted' 'Date: 2026-11-19' 'calcite-cursed-lovebird' 'nonblack-brigandish-guillemot' '## Context' '## Decision' '## Consequences' '## Alternatives' 'verify.trusted_opcert_keys' 'REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS' '<env_id> <key-type> <base64>' 'untrusted' 'trust_list' 'signing_key' 'envelope_key' 'require_environment' 'foreign_key'; do git grep -qF -- "$t" docs/adr/0125-opcert-trust-per-environment.md || echo MISSING "$t"; done` and require no MISSING output. For AC3, add `git grep -n -B3 -A3 'ADR 0125' -- docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md`, with the output showing one hit adjacent to the decision 3 text and one adjacent to the env_id note.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Decision items 3–4, state exactly what 'fails closed' means for a malformed list (verdict name, or ConfigError at config load) and whether that is per certificate or per run; say how that relates to the `foreign_key` refusal when require_environment has no list.
evidence: "a malformed list fails closed"
"without one it refuses with `foreign_key`"
src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py:77 maps `foreign_key` to MINOR
src/rebar/_config_sections.py `_EMPTY_ENV_FAULT_KEYS` already raises ConfigError for bad verify.require_environment overrides
findings.finding: The failure modes are defined unevenly. A missing list under require_environment yields a per-certificate `foreign_key` verdict, while a malformed list only 'fails closed', with no verdict, exit behaviour or scope given. Today `foreign_key` is downgraded to a MINOR finding in `_engine_support/validate.py`, so whether 'fails closed' means a per-cert verdict (which non-gating callers may soften) or a load-time ConfigError (like the empty-env-override faults in `_config_sections.py`) materially changes whether a misconfigured environment fails loudly. The same question applies to a list that is present but has no entry for require_environment's principal.
findings.location: Approach → Decision item 3 ("a malformed list fails closed") and item 4 ("without one it refuses with `foreign_key`")
scenarios: A typo in one MCP-server list entry: does the server refuse to start, return `invalid` for every certificate, or skip the bad entry? Each of the later code, deployment and docs stories could pick a different answer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] List the concrete problems with the current trust root (e.g. keys hardcoded in the repo, bug c21f's own/pinned/embedded fallback) and the positive reason for choosing validity-only plus per-environment lists without eras, so the ADR records the operator's actual rationale.
evidence: "and its problems": no problem is named
Rejected alternatives are listed without reasons; the no-eras rule has no stated benefit (e.g. a single source of truth, simpler revocation) to weigh against what eras would allow
findings.finding: The plan never gives the problems the ADR's Context must describe, or a positive rationale for the chosen design. It says the Context covers today's trust root 'and its problems', and it names rejected alternatives with no reasons. It does not say why validity-only by default plus per-environment lists, with no eras, is the right answer beyond the operator's 'must not be hardcoded' ruling. The ADR author would have to invent the justification for an operator decision.
findings.location: Approach → "Context describes today's trust root (own key, then pinned key, then embedded key; bug c21f) and its problems"; "Rejected alternatives: keep the repo pin file; per-key eras in the list; gating signing on a pinned key."
scenarios: The ADR author writes a rationale the operator never gave (e.g. claims eras are insecure), and future readers cite it as the decision's basis.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Prior art section to ADR 0125 that cites OpenSSH allowed_signers / PROTOCOL.sshsig and git's gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile with its %G? G/U statuses, and state whether `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` entries are a deliberate subset of allowed_signers lines (principal = env_id; options and multi-principal entries allowed or rejected).
evidence: Plan: 'sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives rejected' (no prior-art section)
Plan item 3: 'entries `<env_id> <key-type> <base64> [comment]`'
docs/adr/0044-asymmetric-attestation-substrate.md:130-135 '## Prior art ... OpenSSH `PROTOCOL.sshsig` + `allowed_signers`; git SSH commit signing (`gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile`)'
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:82 `allowed_signers_from_keys` already renders this format
Retrieved: golinuxcloud.com 'Sign and Verify Files with ssh-keygen -Y and allowed_signers'; rya-sge.github.io 'OpenSSH Detached Signatures' ('how allowed_signers decides which keys are acceptable')
findings.finding: ADR 0125's planned structure (Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives rejected) has no Prior art section and never names the established mechanism it re-specifies. That mechanism is OpenSSH allowed_signers, used by git via gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile, which lives in the verifier's own config rather than in the repo, and git's %G? G/U split. The entry format `<env_id> <key-type> <base64> [comment]` is the allowed_signers line without its options field. The `trust_list` vs `untrusted` verdicts match git's 'good' vs 'good signature with unknown validity'.
findings.location: Approach — ADR 0125 sections list; Decision item 3 (entry format)
scenarios: A later story writes its own parser for `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` that differs from allowed_signers (for example on options, multi-principal entries or quoting), and keys copied from existing allowed_signers files are then silently rejected or misread
findings.suggested_fix: Add a '## Prior art' section listing OpenSSH `PROTOCOL.sshsig` + `allowed_signers` (principals/namespaces/valid-after/valid-before) and git SSH signing (`gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` in user config; `%G?` G vs U). In Decision item 3, say the entry format is the allowed_signers line restricted to one principal (the env_id) and say whether options are rejected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In ADR 0125's 'no eras' rule and its rejected-alternatives entry, name allowed_signers valid-after/valid-before and say why per-key validity windows are rejected (for example, no trusted signing time in SSHSIG). Also say whether the OpenSSH 8.9 floor in sshsig.py still has a reason to exist.
evidence: Plan item 3: 'No eras: rotation keeps retired keys listed while their certificates matter; on compromise the key is removed, which untrusts all its certificates.'
src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:36-37 '# OpenSSH 8.9 is the floor: it introduced valid-after/valid-before validity intervals in allowed_signers, which the trust model relies on.'
docs/adr/0044-asymmetric-attestation-substrate.md:94-95 '`ssh-keygen` >= 8.9 is required (the floor for `allowed_signers` validity intervals)'
findings.finding: The rejected alternative 'per-key eras in the list' and the 'No eras' rule don't consider OpenSSH allowed_signers' native per-key valid-after/valid-before options. The repo's SSHSIG substrate explicitly depends on those options (the OpenSSH 8.9 floor exists for them). Under 'no eras', a compromised key can only be removed outright, which untrusts every certificate it ever made, including legitimate ones from before the compromise. Using valid-before is the established middle ground. The plan should justify rejecting it, for example because SSHSIG carries no trusted signing timestamp.
findings.location: Decision item 3 ('No eras ...'); Consequences 'Rejected alternatives: ... per-key eras in the list'
scenarios: After a key compromise the operator must choose between leaving the key listed (forged certificates pass) and removing it (every legitimate historical certificate turns `untrusted`). allowed_signers validity windows exist to avoid exactly that choice

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In ADR 0125 Decision item 2, state how the `envelope_key` check runs (for example, an allowed_signers built from the embedded key passed to `ssh-keygen -Y verify` with the principal and namespace, not `-Y check-novalidate`), and add an ADR 0044 note to Scope if its 'never used for authorization' rule changes meaning.
evidence: Plan item 2: 'the SSHSIG signature verifies under the key embedded in it, for the certificate's principal and the `rebar.opcert.v1` namespace'
docs/adr/0044-asymmetric-attestation-substrate.md:96-97 '`-Y check-novalidate` (structure-only) is never used for authorization.'

Retrieved man7.org ssh-keygen(1): '-Y check-novalidate Checks that a signature generated using ssh-keygen -Y sign has a valid structure. This does not validate if a signature comes from an authorized signer.'
Plan Scope lists only 0125, .numbers/0125, README.md, 0049, 0104
findings.finding: Decision item 2 says default verification checks the SSHSIG signature 'under the key embedded in it', but doesn't say how. ADR 0044 §3 says '`-Y check-novalidate` (structure-only) is never used for authorization.' The man page says check-novalidate 'does not validate if a signature comes from an authorized signer'. A validity-only pass that counts as a successful op-cert verification is in tension with that rule unless the mechanism is stated: synthesize allowed_signers from the embedded key and run `-Y verify`, or use check-novalidate. ADR 0044 is not in Scope for an amendment note.
scenarios: An implementer uses check-novalidate for the `envelope_key` basis, which goes against ADR 0044 and may not enforce the principal binding
A reader of ADR 0044 believes structure-only checks never produce a passing verdict, but under ADR 0125 they do by default

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md to Scope with a one-line note at lines 260-263 saying trusted-environment keys and era validity are now governed by ADR 0125, not ADR 0049.
evidence: docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md:260-261: 'This is the only amendment to ADR 0049. ADR 0049 remains authoritative for Ed25519 and DSSE/SSHSIG, environment attribution, trusted-environment keys and era validity, ...'
Plan Decision 3: 'No eras'; Decision 5: '.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml, rebar trusted-env, and the pin file's log-position key eras are removed'
Plan Scope lists only 0125, .numbers/0125, README.md, 0049 (status line) and 0104 (notes)
findings.finding: ADR 0098 says it is the only amendment to ADR 0049 and that ADR 0049 remains authoritative for 'trusted-environment keys and era validity'. ADR 0125 supersedes repository key pinning and abolishes eras, so after this change ADR 0098 makes a false statement about which ADR governs op-cert trust. The plan's Scope does not list ADR 0098 for a cross-reference note.
scenarios: A reader starting from ADR 0098 follows its statement that ADR 0049 is authoritative for trusted keys and eras, and never learns about ADR 0125's trust-list model.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: `docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md` (one-line note after 'This is the only amendment to ADR 0049': 'ADR 0125 later superseded ADR 0049's repository key pinning and era validity with per-environment trust lists.'). Add an AC: `git grep -n 'ADR 0125' -- docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md` hits that note.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say explicitly that the ADR 0104 note also covers the enforcement-flip text at lines 151-153 and the Consequences bullet at lines 205-206 (flip now also needs the gating environment's `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`), or explain why those are left as historical.
evidence: docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md:151-153: 'The trusted-env / gate slices flip `require_environment` **together with** `opcert_enforce_since` at a deploy-time anchor'
docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md:205-206: 'Enforcement remains advisory until the trusted-env/gate slice flips `require_environment` + `opcert_enforce_since` together'
Plan Decision 4: 'enabling enforcement means setting require_environment, opcert_enforce_since and the list in that environment'
Plan Scope: '`docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` (notes at decision 3 and its env_id note)'
findings.finding: ADR 0104 says in two places, beyond the two spots the plan annotates, that enforcement is enabled by flipping only `require_environment` + `opcert_enforce_since`. Under ADR 0125 Decision 4, a trust list in the gating environment is also required, and without one require_environment refuses with `foreign_key`. These are the decision-3 enforcement paragraph (lines 146-155) and the Consequences bullets (lines 202-207). The plan names neither, so ADR 0104 would still describe a two-setting flip that no longer works.
scenarios: An operator follows ADR 0104's Consequences to enable enforcement, sets only the two settings, and every check is refused with foreign_key because no trust list exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the ADR Decision/Consequences, state that the `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict is removed along with eras, and how existing era-scoped certificates are judged afterwards.
evidence: "No eras: rotation keeps retired keys listed while their certificates matter"
"the pin file's log-position key eras are removed"
src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json verdict enum includes "key_not_valid_at_era"
findings.finding: Removing eras (items 3 and 5) makes the existing `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict, which is in the `verify_signature_result.schema.json` verdict enum, meaningless. The ADR's vocabulary changes list only the additions (`untrusted`, `trust_list`, `signing_key`). It removes the `own_key` and `pinned_environment` trust bases but says nothing about whether `key_not_valid_at_era` is retired or kept, or what happens to stored certificates that would previously have been era-rejected.
findings.location: Approach → Decision items 2/3/5 and Consequences (vocabulary changes)
scenarios: The code story removes eras but leaves `key_not_valid_at_era` in the schema and the MCP tool docs, or keeps an era code path alive, because the ADR never decided.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to item 5: "The `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict is removed; a certificate is judged only by whether its (principal, key) pair is currently listed."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Decision item 3, fix the TOML type of `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` and the entry separator for `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS`, so the item-6 deployment can be written before the parser exists.
evidence: "entries `<env_id> <key-type> <base64> [comment]`" gives the per-entry grammar only; nothing says how entries are separated in the env var or what type the config key has
"This lands before the code stops reading the pin file."
"a malformed list fails closed": a deployment written ahead of the parser in a guessed encoding would fail closed on the MCP server once the parser ships
findings.finding: The ADR does not define how several trust-list entries are encoded in one value of `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` (newline, `;`, comma?) or what TOML type `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` has (array of strings or one multi-line string). Decision item 6 requires the deployment (docker-compose.yml / autodeploy.sh) to be configured with 3 entries BEFORE the code that parses them exists, so the deployment story has to guess a format the later parser may not accept.
findings.location: Approach → Decision item 3 (entry format / env override) and item 6 (land-the-list-first ordering)
scenarios: The deployment story writes the 3 keys into docker-compose as one `;`-joined env var; the code story parses newline-separated entries; the MCP server fails closed and every certificate it checks stops passing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to item 3: "`verify.trusted_opcert_keys` is a TOML array of strings, one entry each; `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` holds the same entries separated by newlines; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored."
